purpose: Two-axes lock 2026-09-17: Axis A = catalog_l1/l2/l3 identity (catalogue, from the declared upstream pr00_classification.csv); Axis B = commercial score beside Axis A (contested per part per market) - not built as scored columns here yet. legacy workbook_l* is context only. Do not invent a fourth layer.
catalog_source_note: catalog_l1/l2/l3 are read LIVE from pr00_classification.csv, the source the master's own cat_* columns are copied from. The master's copy is stale (taken 17 Sep 22:06) and disagrees with that upstream on 2,843 rows. Building from the stale copy would import the drift; building from the declared source does not. Rows where the two disagree are flagged catalog_changed_vs_master=1, so the movement is auditable, not silent.

non_part_rule.matching: normalised: uppercase, spaces removed, leading zeros stripped (the master carries REBATE and 0000REBATE, and LATEPAYMENTINTEREST and 'LATE PAYMENT INTEREST', for the same entities)
non_part_rule.effect: tags line_kind; rows are kept, never dropped. Consumers that want parts revenue filter line_kind=='part'.

consumer_contract: Axis A (identity): group by catalog_l1/l2/l3. Wear and family views hang from catalog_l2/l3 or fig_key - never from a commercial posture parent.
Axis B (commercial score): contested/captive per part per market sits beside Axis A. Never the hang-from parent for identity views.
filter catalog_node_present=1 for a real Axis A family view.
Report catalog_residual=1 (Other / review) as a named residual, never as a family.
workbook_l1 is legacy AIM system context - neither Axis A nor Axis B. Never group workbook_l1 with catalog_l2.
aim_l1_fixed = the governed functional family (what a family question charts).
jp_zkk / jp_zuk are CATALOGUE ATTRIBUTES from the Japan price file. Never chart on them; they are not a family (one code holds 42% of the book across 415 part types).
line_kind != 'part' marks freight / rebate / service-fee / demurrage rows. Filter line_kind=='part' for parts revenue; never let these into a family chart.
